entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Because people lean over before remembering not to answer. Hollow Village draws drinking water elsewhere. The cover keeps children from the edge; the salt needs tending whether the lid is down or not.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Then there is room in your report for what you do not know. Good.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: I say what I’m doing to the person beside me. “Pass the cloth. Hold the bowl.” Real things, with someone there to answer. I don’t work at the boundary alone anymore.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Around the salt, not over it. No ruler has yet improved that instruction.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Walk inside Elin’s salt marks. Your title does not widen them.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Good. The voices under the lid are not survivors waiting to be recruited.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Three drivers came dead with requisition freight from the Old Orchard. The records and tokens are beside the covered Echo Well. I want their names returned to families, not filed under acceptable losses. Keep to Elin’s salt marks; the well speaks, but it cannot testify.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Your council is far away. Here you step around the salt like everyone else.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Three dead drivers arrived with requisition freight from your orchard. I buried them. Their tokens and my notes are by the covered Echo Well. Being taken from elven land did not make them soldiers for either side. Stay inside Elin’s salt marks.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Three dead drivers arrived with requisition freight from the Old Orchard. I buried them; tokens and notes are beside the covered Echo Well. I did not bury them as your subjects or the crown’s. If you want to know who they were, compare Mara’s records. If you want the well to praise you, it will find a voice you like. Do not answer.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: No marching across the salt. Even a burial escort goes around the line.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: The rejects are beside the cold furnace. My name is on them too.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: Yes, my stamp. Burial ash, salt, bell bronze. Some voices in the panes are prisoners holding the Caller out, not the Caller itself. Raut ordered a test at the Glass Quarry. Before you smash every pane, see what happened to the men in the bare frame.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: Look at the bare seat, then the inspector’s signature. Both belong in the same report.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: An inspection? Good. Inspect from behind the chalk like everyone else.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: At the Glass Quarry. There’s room around the cold furnace to compare rejects without anyone carrying molten work past your elbow. The Ash Steppe has plenty of open ground; we still manage to burn ourselves in the crowded bit.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: The quarry keeps the frames and signed test tally. My name stays with the rejects.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: I made the panes. Fitted around a wagon, they work. Bone ash, burial salt and bell bronze hold dead voices that resist the Caller. Loose cargo does not protect its drivers. Raut wanted exclusive supply and charged to cross the danger his requisitions made worse. You could take the books. You would also take the need to keep feeding the furnace.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: A fitted enclosure protects its occupant; loose panels under grain do not. I made it from burial ash, salt and bell bronze. The dead held inside keep the Caller back. Raut’s men tested two frames at the quarry and ordered more. Your escort can survive behind glass while the villages supplying it lose their wards.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: My work bears my stamp, not an oath to your fort. Ask what it does before claiming it.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: You came to question my glass. Stand behind the chalk, even if you hate the answer.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: So the apprentice can see where the crack started. Melt it at once and he’ll make the same mistake with twice the material. I mark my own failures too.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: If you came for a share, first learn whose ship it was. We have enough disputed claims.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: The sacks are gone. The survivors took the lamp too. People here are angry about supper; I’ve told them whose flour we were eating.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: When a rope team can’t stand upright anymore. I send another if I have one. Anyone who promises never to stop has never had to send people out.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: The unsold sacks are under canvas. Nobody touches them until you’ve spoken to Hana.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: You can record our names after we finish warming these survivors. They do not wait for a hearing.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Oss is working under Ivet’s eye while another hand learns the ferry. I heard you did not call useful work an acquittal. Remember that when people ask what my crew did.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: With Oss at a hearing, travelers are taking the long road. I know you are willing to stop useful work while claims are heard. Here, first establish which light the helmsman followed.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: We pulled twelve out. Four are still missing. The helmsman says he saw two lights lining up a channel through the rocks. Hana keeps the true shore lamp. Ask her whether it moved before you let him put all of this on us. I’ve got enough people shouting already.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: We pulled survivors out, not allies. Your banner will not sort the wet blankets.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Ropes from the rocks. Boats would have rolled before we reached it. Wreckers’ Rest keeps shore gear for that. We don’t get to choose whether the sea leaves us men or cargo first.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: They agreed to the loan. Made me count every sack in front of them. Hana holds the tally and the lamp keys now. I’m not allowed to touch a signal alone.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: My crew put it there. They said an empty coaster was coming. I let them, and the coaster wasn’t empty. We’ve eaten some of the flour. I can turn over what remains with our names attached, or ask the survivors to leave it here as a debt while we repair the true warning light. They may refuse. I won’t hide the lamp either way.

Appropriate the shipment for the palace foothold
Secure and supply the palace supply gate
Defeat The Palace Marshal

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Then they may halt your wagons too. We agree on the bells, not on every claim your banner makes.

entries.speaker: elin

Secure and supply the palace supply gate
Defeat Raut

entries.speaker: elin

Defeat The Palace Marshal

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: I consent with the limits understood. Candlekeepers keep access and supplies of their own. Your generosity must not become the only door.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Then clear the road first. Salt and tended bells still protect their own boundaries; the old glass will shelter no long crossing.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Not on your order, or mine. A living keeper would have to understand the confinement and offer freely. I’ve spent long enough studying it to make that choice for myself. No one else owes it to me.

Protect the shipment to the palace supply gate

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: After the actual military victory: palace defended and supplied, living shipment delivered, Raut defeated, and the quarry supplied if pursuit was chosen. Three watches also need Radek’s three bells and Yara’s willing keepers. No order replaces any of those.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text:
Appropriate the shipment for the palace foothold
Secure and supply the palace supply gate
Secure and supply the quarry road
Defeat The Palace Marshal

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Then a village may stop even a palace wagon when its watch fails. Put that beside the promise of support.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Defeat Raut

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text:
Appropriate the shipment and bring it to the Old Fort
Secure and supply the palace supply gate
Defeat The Palace Marshal

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: All three bells must answer before I open it. The villages keep their own ropes, and the right to stop traffic when a watch fails.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Vesk’s authorization is not consent on my behalf. Ask before you reach for the catch.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text:
Secure and supply the forest depot
Secure and supply the palace supply gate
Defeat Raut

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Then clear the exposed routes before we open it. Your comrades need truthful limits more than a proclamation that danger is over.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Then do not name it a gift without naming the cost. Clear the road before opening the anchor; soldiers cannot command the dark to retreat.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: The relief, shipment and sortie must all be complete before this changes. Three bells can replace the anchor if Radek cast three and Yara’s willing watches can feed their dependents. I may freely bind myself instead, confined here for the road. Or we break the glass without replacing it. Vesk can authorize the operation; he cannot make a voice belong to the crown.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text:
Secure and supply the palace supply gate
Defeat The Palace Marshal

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: I know the limit of the gate. No officer signs for my visitors alone, and no missed salute stops my bread.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text:
Repel the attack on the palace supply gate
Protect the shipment to the palace supply gate
Secure and supply the palace supply gate
Defeat Raut

Three bells need three maintained voluntary watches. A living binding needs informed consent and confines its keeper. Breaking it without replacement ends glass protection.

Secure and supply the forest depot

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: If you came to own the binding, first learn what owning it would require of a living person.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: I consent to the fastening, not to your ownership. Let villagers and Candlekeepers both bring food and visitors.

entries.speaker: elin

Secure and supply the forest depot
Defeat Raut

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Complete your campaign first: the live shipment delivered to its chosen destination, the required holdings supplied, the Palace Marshal beaten. Then three willing, maintained watches can replace the anchor if Radek and Yara have made them possible. I may volunteer to bear it, but no conquest constitutes my consent. Or release the dead without replacement and lose the glass shelter. Your victory does not add a fourth mechanism.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text:
Commit to your faction’s military plan
Repel the attack on the palace supply gate
Protect the shipment to the palace supply gate
Secure and supply the palace supply gate
Defeat Raut

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Complete your chosen directive: supply the liberated forest post and, for interdiction, the palace road post too; recover the shipment to the forest and defeat Raut. Then bring workers and provisions. Three independent watches need Radek’s three bells and Yara’s willing keepers; one heavy bell is not a substitute.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Your military victory must be real before anyone opens this catch. Three bells need Radek’s three castings and Yara’s fed, willing watches. I can instead take the binding freely and never leave this cloister. Or we release the dead without a replacement and lose the glass shelter. Freedom is not a spell that keeps a cart safe at night.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: What I saw, then what kept me from seeing the rest. Fog, distance, a blocked lens. An empty gap is better than a confident guess someone will navigate by.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: One light gives a direction. Two aligned lights suggest a channel. That’s why spare red lenses stay locked away, and why I write down the bearing before I turn any screw.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Dren’s crew borrowed a portable lamp to search the shallows. Before the wreck, not after. I saw its red light above the wrong rocks that night and rang the warning, but the ship was already turning. Their lamp had a split carrying sleeve sewn with sail thread. If you find it, compare that seam.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Do not stand between the signal and the sea. Rank does not make you transparent.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: It should be cold enough to handle now. Don’t let anyone call the second light a wandering soul. I know the color of my own lens.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Do not hang a resistance flag on my signal bracket. Ships need the bearing clear.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: The shore light serves ships, including ones you dislike. Leave its bearing alone.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Your title waits outside with your weapons. Inside, the sick take precedence.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: By touch. Cold fingers, poor breathing. People who can still argue about being moved usually aren’t first in need of it.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Raut called it emergency ward-making. Your old freight authority appears beside crown forms in the returns. He took salt, then opened graves. I will keep the remaining consignment here. You can let me circulate the full tally naming his patron, or leave it under witness seal while you trace the buyer. Do not ask me to write that your mountain walls had nothing to do with this.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: I’ll take someone with me to the grave. If the print stops, it tells us he wanted his fare. It won’t tell us whether Oss did right.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: His daughter. I dried her by this stove. She said the ferry swung broadside and her father went over with the safety loop on his wrist. Oss had a knife in his hand. She couldn’t see what he cut. That is all she saw; don’t add to it. The token belongs in the shroud. I can see to that.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Put my name on it. Orsa can compare the quantities against Saltmarket receipts.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Raut’s quartermasters took burial salt and opened graves under emergency papers. Some carried old crown forms. I need the remaining stores at the threshold, and I need their taking recorded somewhere that cannot quietly lose my name. Will you make this an official complaint with a civilian copy, or keep the witnesses confidential in Vesk’s inquiry?

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Sealed, not rewritten. Orsa receives the quantities now. I do not promise to keep your secret forever.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Then Orsa gets the whole tally, too. The remaining salt stays at this threshold.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: They called it emergency ward-making. Burial salt first, then things already in graves. My clothes resemble a guard’s; my patients do not thereby belong to the palace. I have one consignment left. We can refuse it openly, or mark it so Orsa can find the buyer. The second means letting stolen burial stores leave once more.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Bows outside the sickroom. I treat palace conscripts and your wounded on the same clean sheets.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: We dry them, mark where they were found and keep them apart. A recovered coat is not proof its owner drowned. Ask me before taking anything from the shelf.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Your coat opens no priority bed here. The coldest hands go nearest the stove.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Crosses under the handles. I have kept salt for the door; do not let your people call the rest a gift.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Then do not call silence forgiveness. Give Orsa my quantities without the patients’ names.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Then the threshold gets salt tonight. Orsa can work from my tally.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Read the old instructions. They were here before your title and may outlast it.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Tessa says the families moved their bedding before the spring channel opened. You checked where people would live before changing the water. Check who lives at our light before changing its supplies.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: I buried the keeper in spring. Oil still disappears from the supply shelf, and the light still turns in bad weather. No request for wages, no name on the tally. Before someone sends a patrol to stop a theft, would you see who’s up there? A stolen jar is cheaper than a dead traveler.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Star Monastery copied the maintenance instructions, but drawings don’t show every kind of wear. The used parts stay beside them. Ask to compare both before deciding a sketch is complete.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: We keep copies for a reason. A military seal is not our only memory.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Their petition hangs here with my name beneath theirs. The oil is counted openly now. They’re staying at the light while we wait for an answer.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: I can stand surety and ask for civilian service in place of punishment. I cannot grant a pardon, and neither can you. Their names will be posted where officers can read them. Or the Candlekeepers can keep bringing oil quietly, and the three stay hidden. The light gets tended either way; only one lets them ask to come down.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Tessa wrote that repairing the pit cost the workers their wages. Keeping people safe has a supply cost; I cannot pretend the beacon runs on gratitude either.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: I can stand surety and ask the independent witnesses for civilian service in place of punishment. You can decide service in your fort, not erase every claim outside it. Raut’s former men will have their names posted where his officers can read them. Or the Candlekeepers can bring oil quietly and keep the three hidden. The light gets tended either way; only one lets them ask to come down.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Look at the wick trimmings. A lamp left alone burns badly. If they’re fresh, someone is doing the job.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: A bed if they need one. Oil, if they’re working a lamp. My name if they’re accused. I try to find out which of those I’m promising before I sign.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: The oil goes up with the Candlekeepers. Three bowls come back scraped clean. I wish I could offer those people a place at this table as safely.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: You may read the ward books without joining our order. Dry your hands first.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: If it were going to fall on someone. I’ve done it. Kept a sound piece for a stool, burned the rot. Being fond of a tree doesn’t mend its trunk.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: We’ve divided the rows, not the graves. She prunes too hard for my liking. I suppose she’ll say I keep every dead branch. We start together tomorrow.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: The first pay is on my shelf. Feels odd. I can come to the tree whenever I want; the rest of the orchard is hers to manage. I’m trying not to watch.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: You can carry a partisan bow and still hold this graft steady. Help, then talk.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: She could have dug first and argued later. I’ll give her that. Sharing means seeing her at my wife’s tree every morning. Wages mean asking permission to do work I’ve done for twenty years. I can live with either, I think. Which offer would you carry back?

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: The older row breaks the wind for the younger one. I know which branches can go and which will bring a tree down. You can’t learn that by looking at the fruit for one summer.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: They’ve gone to sharpen their tools. That gives you a little time, not much. Don’t pull on a root if you find cloth.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: The woman who bought the orchard isn’t a fool. Half the trees no longer bear, and she paid with the price of her house. But my wife is under the oldest apple tree. When I said so, the cutters called it a trick. There are burial stones under the nettles. Find them before this becomes a fight.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: That sword can stay sheathed. The orchard dispute needs a witness, not a formation.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: If you want fruit, speak to the owner. If you want to talk, hold this twine without pulling.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: No. This is a neutral human inn and I own my wagons. Your order is to protect the living shipment, not destroy it. Your own supply convoy must feed the palace post; pursuit also requires the quarry.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Because if I leave it in the strongbox, sooner or later I’ll call it repair money. Three purses are harder to spend by mistake.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Vesk sent you. Then hear a civilian before you write a military explanation.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: What you own, and what the military operation actually takes. Not every neutral human road stop is a conquered province. Your order seizes a living royal shipment after its guards are beaten; where you take it depends on the command you gave Ren.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: A mountain ruler at my door. The yard is neutral, and the wagons are not a tribute.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: All three identified. Bring the records, not a wreath from an officer who never learned their names.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Then leave me to write to them. Elin is waiting for a ruler to hear a limit.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: The glass stays wrapped. And a guard wearing a palace coat is not proof that every driver serves the palace.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Demand what you like; I did not sell Raut the men beneath his paperwork. Three carts returned, barley untouched, drivers missing, black glass underneath. Here are their token numbers and scars. Toman saw the first man answer his dead wife at the orchard. His bell brought the horses back. I own these wagons. Your quarrel with the crown does not transfer the deeds.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: All three match. I will send their pay home myself. No officer will deduct the cost of missing freight from it. You did this under orders; they still needed somebody to do it.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Tell your commander this part is finished. Elin’s work is not.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Ada’s records name all three. We will speak of them as people, not evidence that your entire side is right.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: I know that forest badge. If your people took my men, say so. Three carts came back with the barley intact and black panels hidden underneath. Here are their pay-token numbers and scars. Toman heard the first man answer his dead wife at the orchard; his handbell brought back the horses, not the men.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: The numbers and the scars agree. All three. I will send the purses home, and I will name them as drivers, not martyrs of a war they never chose. You kept this promise. I have not thereby promised you my next cargo.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: All three match. I will pay their families from the purses I kept. You can conquer the palace and still owe an answer about a freight agent who once worked with your authority. Finding the dead is one answer, not the whole account.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Then go back to Elin. Keep the living off the unwarded stretches while you change anything.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Uniforms loaded my wagons; now a uniform asks where the men went. Here are their token numbers and scars. The carts returned with untouched barley over hidden black glass. Toman saw the lead driver answer his dead wife at the orchard. A bell brought the horses back. Do not write “partisan abduction” because it fits your morning orders.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: The dead have names now. Neither your victory nor Raut’s excuses will replace them.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Then distinguish them when you are holding a sword, too. The tracks are beyond Greenhollow’s salt.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Forest colors. Leave your quarrel outside my yard; the missing men are not prizes.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: The orchard lies outside Toman’s tended salt. Mind where you put those regulation boots.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: By agreement, with the drivers told what they carry. Roadward is a neutral human inn, not a partisan depot. Your own convoy must supply the posts you take.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: She called me Mila over breakfast. Then cried into the porridge. I stayed. The mittens fit, by the way.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: You may command a fort. This coat belongs to someone who asked me not to cut it down.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: Do you need this coat mended or its former owner judged? I can do the first.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: We’ve spoken about the grave. She still uses the old name sometimes. I answer her when she’s beside me, not when something calls through the door. The neighbors can ask if they want to know.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: She measured my hand while I slept. I thought she was checking my fever. So she knows, and neither of us can bring ourselves to say it. I can ask her to call me Mila. Or let the old pet name stay between us, if we finally speak about whose grave the candle goes to. She may cry all night. I’ve been avoiding that more than the truth.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: The door stays barred. I tell her it’s cold. She tells me she knows. I don’t know which of us thinks that fools anyone.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: Alya died on the road. I brought her scarf to her mother. The fever had left the old woman weak; she saw it on my shoulders and called me by Alya’s pet name. I stayed to nurse her. Never corrected her properly. Now Alya’s voice calls outside. Her mother left a bundle at the Echo Well. Please see whether it’s meant for a living girl or a dead one.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: I can mend a uniform. I cannot make its former owner’s promises fit the next person.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: Some. People leave candles and things to take to the graves. I sew covers so they stay dry. Don’t move a bundle just to read what’s underneath; someone will think it’s been taken.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: Because cutting it down is easy. Asking whether they want it cut is harder. Sometimes they still want the old shoulders in it for a while.

entries.text: No Rival’s Glass

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Ivet kept her stores and agreed to confidential testimony. The evidence has independent copies, but public scrutiny of the command must wait.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Missing Warning
Yara left the bell with the displaced households and concealed their shelter from the patrol. They retain a close warning, but no common watch forms around the shrine.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Scarf That Came Back
Mila and the mother acknowledged Alya’s death but kept the household pet name. They know not to answer the voice outside. Their private comfort remains difficult to explain to neighbors.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: One returned bell yoke has an empty crown where its bronze was sawn away. Its village complaint lists disappearances after the removal. Raut marked the complaint “received” before renewing the same requisition. His personal share of paid escorts rises in the following weeks. A scorched courier tube holds a refused request to consult the old ward instructions at Star Monastery. This is not an inspector acting alone.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The Palace Marshal falls and your chosen military claims are fulfilled. Behind supplied holdings, with the living shipment safely delivered, the crews clear the road and break the anchor. The dead leave. No rival can purchase Raut’s glass advantage now, and no captive replaces it. Your soldiers can take a tollhouse but cannot order the Caller away from an exposed cart. Freight moves in daylight, fees rise and two distant hamlets empty before winter. The Old Fort gains an enemy’s defeat, not command of the night. Mara pays the drivers’ families and refuses to call their loss part of your triumph. You have destroyed a rival source of power. The people who must travel through what remains will decide what else to call it.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Six low stones follow the oldest row. Each names a burial; the planting dates are later. A storm-torn root holds shroud cloth, not a fresh body. The new survey pegs run straight across the graves. Felling and grubbing this row would disturb the burials, but the younger trees beyond it remain productive. Nothing here shows a curse.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Three Pairs of Boots
Lev publicly stood surety for the three keepers and petitioned for civilian service. Their names and Nika’s account are available to witnesses. A promise of safe escort has not erased the charges against them.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A keeper’s copper wrist-piece is worn smooth on the inside. The servicing sketches show it fastened to a glass anchor at the Old Cloister, in Hollowvale. A living volunteer once bore the binding; later hands substituted the dead. Three independent bell watches can take over if all are maintained before the anchor is opened. Without either arrangement, breaking the anchor releases its captives and ends the glass protection. Repairs annotated over several generations agree with the wear on the fittings.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Water drips through a roof of woven reeds. Beside the altar, rescued clothing has been spread over benches to dry.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Iron-bound doors stand beneath the old storehouse. Wax flakes litter the steps, and damp has darkened the planks of the packing crates inside.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Vesk authorized pursuit. The palace relief and living shipment escort remain mandatory; capture and supply of the quarry are an additional duty before the fortress sortie.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The Charter of Three Watches

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Vesk approved an open muster and put his own signature beside the findings. The garrison heard the evidence before its ordered sortie.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The wicks are neatly trimmed. Three sets of wet boots dry beside narrow bunks; army patches have been cut from the coats above them. The watch tally changes hand every four hours. A rescuer’s rope is abraded where it ran over ice, and a child’s mitten is drying beside it. Three people are working here. Cut patches suggest desertion, but do not explain why they left.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Ivet refused the shipment. I supported a neutral chapel’s refusal, not an elven claim over its stores.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Scarf That Came Back
Mila and the older woman spoke plainly about Alya’s death and began using Mila’s own name at home. They remain together. Naming the loss brought grief back into the room; it did not undo it.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Second Shore Light
The survivors allowed the food to remain as a witnessed debt, not lawful salvage. Dren’s crew must repair the warning equipment under Hana’s eye. The injured sailors still lack payment for what they lost.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Enough Bronze for Three
The bronze remains in storage. Radek cannot promise three village bells, and no one has agreed to collect or tend them.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: White stones mark the edge of an old burial mound. Ash has filled the shallow drainage channel, and dead grass clings to the damp bank.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: One Door Left Shut

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I chose dominion: capture and supply palace and quarry, appropriate the living shipment and deliver it to the palace post before defeating the Palace Marshal. I mean to hold what I take.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Enough Bronze for Three
Radek cast one heavy bell for the busy crossing and returned the village deposits. Its single watch cannot replace the three separate watches required to free the road from one central binding.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The bell hangs from a low beam above five bedrolls. Its clapper is unwrapped; a fresh salt boundary encloses the sleepers. A woman shows the blister the hauling rope left on her palm. She agrees to return the bell to the shared frame if someone keeps watch there and meals are set aside for those who cannot take a turn. No one offers to leave the children alone again.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: An overturned hull shelters salvage crews. Wet boots steam by the stove, and salvaged lanterns crowd a shelf above the bunks.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The three pay tokens match Mara’s numbers. Ada’s burial notes describe the same old scars Mara recorded. The drivers are dead; what killed them remains uncertain. Bone grit and shroud-thread cling beneath the washing ledge. Black splinters catch in the overflow, where a copper conduit leads toward the Old Cloister. Below the lid, a voice asks for the lead driver’s coat in the words Toman heard. That voice is not evidence of a survivor.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Two cart frames stand on the test bed: one glazed, one bare. Both salt lines were deliberately broken. Only the bare frame’s seat bears rope burns. The dated tally records two handlers lost from that frame after answering voices; the man inside the glazed frame remained at his post. Raut’s inspector countersigned the test and ordered another batch. Crushed coffin fittings remain in the mixing trough. Beran’s account, the chapel freight and the shipment weights fit together. The panels work as a fitted enclosure, not as loose cargo beneath grain sacks.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Vesk’s order is fulfilled: the palace stands, its shipment survives and Raut falls. With the route secured, Elin freely takes the binding and sends the captive dead away. Palace stores support him, while Candlekeepers retain independent access. For the guards it looks at first like a familiar posting: a gate, a ration, a watch. Then the first relief roster arrives with nobody able to replace his name. Comrades bring news and repair the roof; none can give him leave beyond the worn gate stone. Mara pays the families of her drivers. The road works, and the garrison must live with the difference between honoring a volunteer and making his sacrifice convenient.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The council published the requisition evidence, including Vesk’s role. We refused to make our village witnesses subordinate to a useful palace contact.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Second Shore Light
The remaining cargo went to the surviving crew, with the false lamp and Dren’s account. The shore households must replace the food already eaten; the deaths are still for witnesses to judge.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Enough Bronze for Three
Radek cast the three small bells and set them aside for the villages. They can support separate watches using the Old Cloister fittings, but they still need willing keepers and a secured delivery route.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Thorn scrub fills the ground floor of a ruined watchtower. An old signal chain hangs through the stairwell, its lowest links polished by use.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Your army holds the royal citadel. The terms of your rule now belong to you, not an employer.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The palace assault is repelled, the living shipment delivered and Vesk’s assigned operation completed. Raut is defeated in the ordered sortie. Radek’s three bells and Yara’s willing watches take over before Elin releases the dead. Vesk recognizes their right to halt a military convoy when salt is wet or a rope fails. Some officers call that surrendering authority. The sentries call it a reason to get home. The crown has kept its palace without acquiring every road as property. Mara pays the three families; the garrison records their names without awarding itself credit for their deaths. The charter needs stores, replacements and commanders willing to obey its limits.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Floodwater has left a brown line above the stone shelves. Swollen boxes rest in the mud, with brass fittings green from the damp.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Narrow arches overlook the snowfields. Candle grease coats the reading desks, and a worn bell rope passes through a hole in the ceiling.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Vesk assigned relief: repel the palace attack, supply the palace post and bring the protected shipment there alive, then undertake the fortress sortie. Quarry occupation is not part of this order.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Roots Below the Deed
I carried Lida’s acceptance of shared cultivation. The graves remain untouched. Both women have a claim on the harvest and a reason to argue over the work.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Ivet kept her remaining stores and lodged a named complaint with an independent copy. Vesk’s office must now answer a record it cannot withdraw alone.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Hairline cracks run through the old bell crowns beneath the soot. Striking them gives a dull double note. Once the iron yokes and ruined fittings are deducted, Radek’s chalk estimates fit: three small recast bells or one heavy bell with a spare clapper. The village deposits are separate from the unsigned garrison offer. The shortage is real, not a duplicate sale.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I retained my claim to requisition living military supplies while exposing Raut’s use of graves and private fees. The distinction is public, but leaves broad power in my own hands.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I publicly renounced the old burial-requisition authority Raut used. This limits one instrument of my rule; it does not cancel my military ambition or absolve my earlier delegation.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The crate holds salt-caked shrouds, coffin nails with wood still on them, and sacks of pale bone ash. A black panel fits its padded lid. The outward tag names Reed Chapel; the return tag names a furnace shipment through Saltmarket. These were not unused burial supplies. Someone collected them from graves, packed them carefully and sent glass back in the same crates.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Fallen apples soften in the cart ruts. A broken fence borders the oldest trees; several branches bear deep rope marks.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Three Pairs of Boots
Lev arranged quiet supplies through the Candlekeepers. The beacon remains tended, but its keepers still cannot visit the settlements without risking arrest.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I allowed the chapel to circulate the full account of Raut’s use of my authority. I did not gain innocence by exposing a former agent.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Fare on the Step
Oss gave Ivet his account and stayed to train a replacement under her oversight. The family crosses without payment. Returning the token ended the wet prints; it did not settle responsibility for the cut rope.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
What Boiling Leaves Behind
The workers stopped the washing line to repair the settling pit. Tessa will keep the lower well closed until repeated checks are clear. The lost wages are immediate; recovery is not.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Scarf That Came Back
Mila stays in the household under the dead girl’s pet name. The two women still have not spoken plainly about the grave.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
What Boiling Leaves Behind
The cellar households moved into the loft before the clean spring channel was opened. The washing line continues, but the polluted well stays closed. Families have water and wages at the cost of their separate rooms.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The Forest Takes the Night

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The relief succeeds, the shipment reaches the palace alive and the authorized sortie defeats Raut. Only after the road is cleared do the crews break the binding. The dead are released; no conscript is ordered into their place. Vesk signs daylight timetables and accepts that a military seal cannot protect wagons between tended boundaries. Patrols grow longer, leave shorter. A winter delivery turns back, and palace tables lose luxuries before the garrison admits it cannot promise every distant village the same cover. Mara pays the missing drivers’ families and demands honest risk clauses. The guard has kept its oath by naming what it can defend, not by declaring everything defended.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Raut is defeated, the intercepted shipment has reached the forest and the council’s chosen front is supplied. Radek’s three bells reach Yara’s willing watches. Only when every bell answers does Elin release the dead. Greenhollow keeps its wooden hall, not a new palace. The villages can refuse troops, but must also feed the households that keep watch. A harvest dispute closes one stretch for two days. Traders complain; the council will not compel a hungry family to ring. Mara pays the drivers’ families and bargains for passage as an independent carrier. The forest has won the right to answer for itself, not the right to stop answering others.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Black glass chips are ground into the sling beside barley husks. A broken panel is grooved to fit a wagon’s covered frame, not a window. The maker’s stamp matches a delivery docket from Cinderwell; the buyer is Raut’s convoy office. The burial crates traveled back empty of glass and heavy with chapel freight. The loading weights confirm both journeys.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Ice grips the iron signal basket. Freshly split kindling lies beneath its cover, beside a watch stool wrapped in sheepskin.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Black slag lies among broken furnace bricks. Wheel tracks run between the cooling pits, where discarded molds are stacked under torn canvas.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The yoke pins were withdrawn with a proper iron drift, not broken. Wool wrapped around the clapper kept it quiet. Two deep adult boot tracks lead toward the rear of the shrine; a drag mark stops at stone paving. A strip of flour-sack cloth hangs on the frame. Whoever took the bell meant to use it intact.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Under the unsold sacks lies the red lamp, wrapped in a split sleeve repaired with sail thread. Its foot is packed with the same white grit as the false bearing above the rocks. Fresh oil remains in the reservoir; the lens’s copper rim bears the observatory’s equipment mark. Beside it are tally sticks dividing the cargo before any salvage hearing. The lamp and repaired sleeve match Hana’s account. Who set the false light still needs to be established.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The bundle contains a candle tied with Alya’s hair ribbon and a pair of newly knitted mittens. The candle paper reads “For Alya’s grave”; the mittens are wrapped in a note: “Mila, these should fit this time.” There is no food for a returning traveler. The mother knows who died and who is living in her house. The voice outside has not changed that.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A corroded brass gauge stands beside the tower steps. The lantern housing is scored by windblown sand; old tide marks stripe the lower stones.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The council chose interdiction. In addition to recovering the shipment to the forest and defeating Raut, we must capture and supply both the forest and palace road posts.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Three sets of bootprints leave the wheel ruts. None returns. A torn salt pouch hangs from the lead cart’s broken rail; rain has washed a gap through the spilled line. Under a sackcloth scrap lies black glass wrapped in linen stitched for a burial shroud. A brass shipping tag bears the mark of Reed Chapel. There is no blood or sign of a struggle.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Ivet consented to one marked consignment. We gained a trail at the expense of her remaining linen; this was not costless solidarity.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A Throne with Three Limits

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Weathered antlers crown the shrine gate. Bowls of porridge and patched blankets lie beneath a bare wooden bell frame.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: With the forest post supplied and the resistance’s chosen campaign won, the crews break the anchor after clearing the road. The dead leave; no living prisoner replaces them. Raut’s glass no longer buys passage. Neither does a forest badge keep the Caller out between tended boundaries. Partisans guide daylight convoys and return to their farms exhausted. Two exposed hamlets move inside Greenhollow before winter; the orchard loses land to new houses. Mara pays the three families and writes risk payments into her next contract. The forest has refused to live on captive voices. It will not get back everything that refusal costs.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The council chose shelter. We must liberate and supply the forest post, recover the intercepted shipment there and defeat Raut. We do not require a further palace-post occupation.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I asked for delayed publication while independent witnesses retained the evidence. Raut’s victims must wait; control of the timing serves my campaign as well as the inquiry.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I chose plunder: take and supply the palace post, bring the appropriated living shipment back to the Old Fort, then defeat the Palace Marshal. Quarry occupation is not required.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Frayed cords descend into the dark shaft. Two clay bowls stand on the curb, and a loose stone rattles far below when the wind turns.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Vesk approved closed, complete briefings for the sections. Comrades receive the truth, but civilians must wait for the command’s public account.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A brass fare token is sewn inside the coat lining. A length of ferry safety rope was preserved with it: one end snapped into fibers, the other was cut cleanly. The burial label says the body was recovered downstream with a loop still around its wrist. The token was not buried with him. The cut alone does not say why it was made.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The Uncrowned Watches

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I concealed Vesk’s cooperation while keeping independent copies. The villages must wait to question him; the resistance now owes them an explanation.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The glass anchor sits in a copper cradle, patched with the same black castings found in Raut’s freight. Burial cloth is fused into its layers. Elin briefly closes the old wrist-piece around his hand: the voices recede into a single strained breath. He opens it before the fastening catches. Three unused bell connections surround the cradle; their spacing matches the monastery sketches. All three alternatives require workers and supplies from outside. Opening the fastening before they arrive would leave the road unprotected.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The Palace Marshal is defeated at the royal citadel. The appropriated shipment has reached the destination you chose, and your required holdings stand supplied. You remain the ruler of the Old Fort, not a rewarded servant of the crown. Radek’s three bells reach Yara’s willing watches; Elin releases the dead only when every bell answers. Independent communities keep the ropes and can stop even your wagons when a watch fails. Ren calls the bargain a durable road, not a surrender. Some retainers call it three small refusals a conqueror ought not tolerate. You tolerate them because reliable passage serves your power better than Raut’s furnace monopoly. Mara pays the drivers’ families, and their records still carry the history of your former agent.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Second Shore Light
The salvaged cargo is sold a little at a time. The helmsman’s account of the second light remains untested.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Fare on the Step
Oss leaves the last crossing empty. The wet print keeps returning, and the passenger’s family has no account of his death.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
What Boiling Leaves Behind
Tessa carries water from farther uphill for the worst cases. The source of the contamination remains in use.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Fare on the Step
Oss agreed to an immediate hearing and suspended his crossings. Ivet returned the token and the prints stopped. Travelers must use the longer land route while another ferryman is sought.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Fir needles cover the roofless passage. A stone worktable survives beside the ruined chapel, its surface scarred by clamps and scorched wax.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Missing Warning
The Stag Shrine remains silent. Yara has no common watch to offer the road, and the scattered households fend for themselves.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Missing Warning
Yara and the families restored the shrine bell together. Hunters volunteered for a shared watch after meals were guaranteed for their dependents. These are willing allies for a future network, not people assigned to it.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Your military campaign succeeds against the Palace Marshal; the live prize is delivered and the chosen holdings are supplied. Elin freely closes the wrist-piece and releases the dead. Your standards now travel under a ward centered on one man who cannot pass the cloister gate. You provision him and gain the reputation of a ruler who can make roads work. Candlekeepers keep another key and a separate store; without them every petition could become a request for your favor. Ren records the upkeep beside the revenues, refusing to call the keeper spoils. Mara pays the three families. Raut’s papers survive in independent hands: conquering a palace has not rewritten the authority that once helped him.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The forest wins its military campaign, but its victory has one boundary that cannot be opened. Elin willingly closes the wrist-piece and releases the captive dead; he can walk only as far as the cloister gate. The road keeps its shelter. Toman refuses a proposal to put a partisan sentry in sole charge of Elin’s visitors. Candlekeepers hold a second key and independent stores, yet every winter someone must cross hostile ground to replenish them. Mara sends the drivers’ wages home. Children in Greenhollow grow up hearing that no ruler owns them. When they ask why Elin cannot come to the harvest feast, the adults must tell the whole story.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Roots Below the Deed
Lida accepted wages while the buyer kept the deed. Toman witnessed unrestricted access to the graves. The burials are safe, but Lida no longer decides what happens to the living orchard.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Three Pairs of Boots
The monastery keeps sending oil to an unanswered post. Whoever tends the beacon has no promise of another winter’s supplies.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The occupation is broken. Your decisions determine how the households survive the Hollow Road.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A split settling pit leaks gray furnace wash directly into the lower well feeder. Upstream stones are clean; below the leak they carry a pale metallic crust. The older spring channel remains clear behind a silted sluice. Opening it would give clean water a separate route, but its overflow passes through the rooms workers have made in the old cellar. The leak, the deposits and Tessa’s cases point to ordinary poisoning.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The defense, protected delivery and authorized sortie are complete. Your service record shapes the settlement.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Old lime seals across the lamp bolts are unbroken. Its beam still meets the channel marker on the same bearing. A spare red lens is missing from the rack; its socket has fresh copper filings. The fixed light was not moved. A second portable lamp could have made a false alignment, but the empty rack does not identify who used it.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Roots Below the Deed
The sale remains disputed. Lida tends the trees she can reach; the oldest row goes unpruned while both households wait.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The Keeper and the Conqueror

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Lev has it at Star Monastery, with the worn fittings that explain the drawings.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: It gives a bearing, not a path. Follow the markers through High Pass even when the light looks close. Frostspine folds the ground between you and it into places you can’t see until you’re in them.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Then keep someone beside your proudest soldier. He may need a hand before he admits it.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Raut broke the monastery seal in front of me, read the warning and asked only how many wagons the glass covered. On our return the courier answered her dead brother. I held her coat until she stopped climbing off the path. Your regulations need someone close enough to catch a comrade, not merely a rule against answering.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: I’ll sign for the boy and the rope. Not for battles I wasn’t at. That should still count for something.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Often. Cold makes people certain there’s a warm house just below the next ledge. A familiar voice can do worse. Get them somewhere sheltered first. Argue once they can feel their hands.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Then use the marked path. A partisan can fall off a cliff as readily as a soldier.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: The pass is not yours because your fort overlooks it. I guided the courier who warned Raut. He read the letter, then asked how much freight his glass could cover. On the way back she answered her dead brother. I held her coat until she stopped stepping off the path. A commander may order silence; grief does not salute. Lev has the old fittings and the warning at Star Monastery.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Your comrade has numb fingers. Warm them before saluting anybody.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Raut read the warning in front of me and asked how many wagons his glass could cover. On the way back the courier answered her dead brother below the path. I held her coat until she stopped climbing down. Your anger will not make that voice less persuasive. Lev kept the warning and the old fittings at Star Monastery.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: You can see your fort from here. You still need a guide on this side of the ridge.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Another person from the low woods. Up here a familiar accent is not a safe path.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: I’ve seen all three. Two hauled a boy out of a drift while the third kept the light. They left Raut’s unit after an order to strip salt from occupied houses. That part is their account; the rescue I saw myself. They’ll sign a petition if Lev stands surety. They won’t walk unguarded into the barracks.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Conquest changes who asks for credit. It does not change how much grain is in a sack.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: I will not sell you a neat distinction between Raut’s profits and the power that opened his doors. The Tide Observatory has a broken panel and a sling that carried twice the declared barley weight. Check them. Buying the road does not make the accounts disappear.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: If the palace needs another load, it needs another honest account of what is inside.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Which load do you dispute? Not every wagon beyond the forest belongs to your enemy.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Seed, sometimes. Supper, I call a gift if I can afford it. Calling a gift a loan makes people hide from you at the worst possible time.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: A forest blockade will not tell me who paid. The Tide Observatory kept the damaged barley freight and its weighing sling. Compare them before you stop my other loads. Neutral customers eat those.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Saltmarket weighs the sale. The Tide Observatory weighs what a boat can actually lift without sinking. On the Salt Coast I prefer to compare the two before I pay for a missing half-ton.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Keep the packing. A slogan is light; hidden glass is not.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: The declared barley weight does not match the sling at the Tide Observatory. You can guard a load faithfully and still guard a lie. Check the damaged panel and the buyer’s docket before calling this secure supply.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: That distinction may keep another driver alive. The sling is on the lower shelf.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: And the maker’s mark leads inland. Neither is impressed by titles.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: I’ve tied the boat up before sunset. First time in years I’ve been early for anything.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: A mountain fort cannot order this river level down. Wait for my signal to board.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: Same handprint every dusk. No feet coming up to it. I scrub the step; it comes back. A man drowned here in the spring flood. The chapel has his things. See whether they kept his fare token. Maybe I’ve been leaving the wrong coin.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: My account is with the witnesses. The boat stays tied; I won’t take another fare while they hear it. No wet hand on the step now. Just people asking when they can cross.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: No print since the burial. Ivet checks the crossings, and the new hand is learning the knots. The girl takes the free passage. She sits at the far end.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: I cut it. The loop caught the rudder and held us across the current. There were four others in the boat. I could have tried another knot; I didn’t. His daughter knows where to find me. Ivet will hear my account with witnesses. I can go now and tie up the ferry, or stay under her oversight and teach another hand before I leave.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: Lantern Ferry has a crosscurrent you can see by day. After dark you only feel it when the boat turns. The shore bell warns of things on the bank; it doesn’t steer for you.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: A command voice will not slow the current. Step where I show you.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: No ambush on my ferry. Whoever is on the plank gets to the other bank first.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: When the water reaches the second peg. Used to measure with my boot instead. The pegs don’t change their mind when someone offers more.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Their families owe the resistance nothing. Keep the originals.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep it. Our resistance will not demand your last salt.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Stay under Ivet’s oversight and teach a replacement. Give the family free passage, not excuses.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What will you recognize as mine?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Cast the three village bells. I’ll carry your terms to anyone asking for them.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Go to the hearing now. Leave the ferry tied until another ferryman is found.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: III. The Price of Command

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll follow the channel and look for where the two waters meet.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Mark one last load, with your consent. We need the buyer, not a scapegoat.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Ask her to use Mila. Take the candle together; you don’t have to leave her.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: IV. A Power Not Borrowed

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I will inspect the old work. I have no use for a defense that depends on pretending men do not grieve.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll give Radek the actual weights and both terms.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I will compare the identifying marks and preserve your uncertainty about the cause.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll look beneath the nettles. Ask the cutters to wait.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I claim the royal shipment, not your title to every cart. I will inspect the orchard.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Load what remains for the survivors. I’ll carry the lamp and your account with it.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The escort order does not exempt the cargo from inspection.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll look for his belongings at the chapel. Don’t make another night crossing alone.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Move the bedding first, then open the spring channel. No one sleeps below the overflow.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How much does it cost you to stand surety for someone?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I. Under My Own Standard

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why open the vault to an opposing ruler?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep identities confidential for now; preserve copies outside the command desk.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why send freight to the Tide Observatory to be weighed?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The records are yours. The wages are not military salvage.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why let a partisan see your records?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Circulate it. My claim to rule will have to survive my name on the page.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The purses remain theirs. My campaign does not inherit their pay.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Show me the test, including your own part in it.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why is the mill open after dark?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: V. A Road the Forest Can Refuse

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: II. A Seal Is Not an Answer

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The accounts stay. I want to know what power he was buying.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: V. After the Watch Is Relieved

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Publish both signatures. A truce is not a pardon.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll ask Lev to stand surety and include what you actually witnessed.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep flawed castings instead of melting them again?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll check the shelter without bringing the patrol.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why not simply order every hunter to take a watch?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep the pet name if you both want it. But tell her whose candle you’re carrying.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep old ward fittings alongside the books?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Would you cut down a tree you planted yourself?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: We did not take them. I will follow the tracks and give you the evidence.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Renounce that writ. I will take territory openly, not claim the dead as freight.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep his channel open until the road is secured. Preserve copies outside the palace.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I did not come for your permission to rule. I will read the records.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Does a fine bell protect a village by itself?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Will you contradict me in front of the retainers?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I will carry your account with the monastery copy.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Have you ever dragged someone back who begged to go on?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Request an open muster. The ranks can bear the truth better than another rumor.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep tending trees that no longer bear?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Accept the paid care. Have Toman witness your right to reach the graves.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Your account goes in the report unchanged. I will examine the tracks.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Three Pairs of Boots

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: End the captive ward. We will guard daylight routes without claiming the glass still protects them.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Publish his deviations. Retain my authority over living military supply.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll look through the salvage for the lamp and sleeve.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How do you choose who gets the bed nearest the stove?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Plunder. Supply the palace foothold, but bring the living prize to my mountain walls.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: When can I take a road shortcut with the convoy?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can a ship mistake a house lamp for a channel light?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I. Walls That Burn

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Accept Elin’s voluntary binding, with no council holding his only key.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Does an order excuse taking our grain?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Do you ever refuse a fare?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Accept your voluntary service. Keep provisioning and access in separate hands.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Dominion. Hold palace and quarry; make the captured shipment supply my advance.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep their names private. Ask the Candlekeepers to keep the oil coming.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Request section briefings with complete copies. No falsified account to the ranks.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I answer to the households. I will identify the load before we strike.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Interdict: hold and supply both forest and palace road posts.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can loyalty require a report against our own command?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What makes you refuse a cart that the driver says is sound?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: III. Our Own Signatures

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Orders understood. I will return the people and the evidence, not just the standards.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep independent sealed copies. I want the buyer before the public accusation.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll look at the bundle. Keep the door closed, even if the voice sounds kind.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Will you carry supplies for the resistance?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How do you tell sickness from the Caller’s work?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The citadel is my target. No crown commission will settle this campaign.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Set aside food for their dependents. I’ll back the families’ place in the shared watch.

entries.text: The Scarf That Came Back

entries.speaker: player

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I need to go.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Register the complaint and leave an independent copy with the chapel.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What military obligations remain?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Return the token to him. I’ll ask Oss about the cut rope.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Would you go under for something that cannot be sold?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can you mend a cracked bell without recasting it?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Accept independent watches. A road with limits is worth more to my rule than Raut’s monopoly.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What do you put in the log when you aren’t certain?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll inspect the shore lamp first. Keep the remaining cargo together.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Shelter: free and supply the forest post; bring the intercepted shipment home.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why mend a coat that will never fit its new owner?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Take the binding by your own offer. I will provision the cloister, but cannot own your consent.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I will enter both names and preserve the original returns.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Recommend relief. Our comrades and the shipment come first.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll examine the stored pieces before you choose a casting.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I will inspect the test. “It works” does not settle what we may use.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: No forest crown for me. Secure the road, then let the households judge its future.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Give me the records. I will not count a borrowed voice as an oath.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What is my duty at the palace post?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Show me the test. I will not call dependence on a furnace sovereignty.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Are the cloth bundles by the well yours?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What must the resistance secure before the binding changes?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll check the frame. Keep the patrol away from the children until then.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What does Thornwatch watch besides hunters?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Only the requisition column is our target. I will check the sling.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Cast the heavy crossing bell. Return the village deposits in full.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: When do you stop looking for a missing sailor?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How do you keep working when it calls in a voice you know?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Do you ever leave someone outside when the mill is full?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: V. The Victor’s Road

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I need the crate, not an invented oath. Show me the safe approach.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Is Roadward part of the palace supply command?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How did your crew reach the wreck through the breakers?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I want evidence, not your oath.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can the Frozen Beacon be trusted in this weather?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Leave the bell with the families. Keep the patrol away from their shelter.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Where does the seized shipment go under my command?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Back the stoppage and repair the pit. Keep carrying spring water until the well is safe.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The Roots Below the Deed

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep the missing drivers’ pay separate?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Tell her you’ll share the work and the fruit. Keep the burial row out of the bargain.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I choose the targets. Bring me the freight trail, not a royal employment offer.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Recognize independent watches. The garrison supports them without owning their ropes.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I will compare the names, not claim the dead for our cause.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why does the Echo Well stay covered?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Where do you test a new casting?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What happens to the things brought in from the river?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Would you put another person into that fastening?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Do you lend grain to people who might not repay it?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Recommend pursuit. Relieve the palace, then take and supply the quarry.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The Missing Warning

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Understood. I will establish what happened before naming an enemy.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Will you serve whoever wins the citadel?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What Boiling Leaves Behind

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: When may the guard carry out the ward operation?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I accept access, not your authority over Greenhollow.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll take both offers to Lida. Keep the grave boundaries marked.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Give the watches to the villages, never to a forest throne.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Ask for a food loan, openly. If they agree, have Hana witness the debt and the repair work.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What are you comparing in those jars?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can anything still be recovered from the Drowned Archive?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: IV. No New Master

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What limits remain after I defeat the palace?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll inspect the watch before anyone cuts off its oil.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The dead are not our scouts. I will compare the fittings.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Release every captive. We accept the exposed road instead of another keeper.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: II. Graves on the Freight List

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: You are a witness, not a suspect for refusing an oath.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Break the monopoly and the glass together. I accept an exposed road no rival can buy from Raut.

entries.text: III. Axes and Orders

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why tie up the ferry before the water gets dark?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Stand surety. I’ll add Nika’s account and escort their petition, not promise a pardon.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: I heard the families kept their bell. Fair enough, but that leaves Yara without a shared watch. I can still cast three village bells, if someone later finds willing keepers, or one heavy bell for the busy crossing. Metal won’t decide who gets up in the night.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: A royal request cannot make one bell ring in three villages. We will count the metal first.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Three small bells will carry between nearby watches, if people keep the ropes and salt in order. I can cast them to the Old Cloister fittings. The heavy one will sound farther from a single crossing and need fewer hands, but the outlying houses won’t hear it. I won’t sell either as protection without someone there to ring it.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Vesk has the key and the weights. If he quotes the total without the iron, ask him to weigh it again.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Yara wrote about her rota and the meals for dependents. That is the first offer of keepers I can put a casting against. Three small bells would suit their shared watches and the Old Cloister fittings. One heavy bell serves a single crossing better. Choose the use before I pour; I can’t turn one into three afterward.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Three villages paid deposits on funeral bells. Then the garrison offered to buy one big warning bell out of the same bronze. I haven’t promised the metal twice. I haven’t seen all of it yet. The returned pieces are in the Sealed Vault. Tap the crowns, not the skirts. It’s the part that holds the weight I need to know about.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: The bronze is already spoken for under witnessed terms. Your arrival does not melt those terms.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: No. Someone checks the rope, clears the ice and takes the night turn. The bronze is my work. I make that part sound and tell them plainly what is theirs.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Three sound crowns. I’ve tested each one. They’re waiting for the watches and the wagons now. Tell Elin I kept to the old measurements; tell everyone else to bring dry rope.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Bronze has no loyalty to the forest or the palace. A cracked crown will drop either bell.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Sometimes a skirt. Not a split crown that has to carry the whole weight. At the Bell Foundry we keep the failed crowns on view. It discourages people from hanging bells with repairs they made in a hurry.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: The heavy bell rings true. The deposit money has gone back. It will do a useful job at one crossing. Not three jobs in three villages.

entries.speaker: ren

entries.speaker: ren

First, a warning: Raut used your old freight authority to move black panels under barley. Mara’s previous drivers disappeared. Learn what we are taking before we put it inside your walls.

entries.speaker: ren
entries.text: The sketches offer three maintained bell watches, a willing confined keeper, or broken glass with no replacement shelter. None hands you effortless mastery. Radek must cast three bells and Yara must find willing, fed watches for the first. Your military order remains yours: deliver the seized living shipment to the palace under dominion, or bring it back here under plunder; supply the required holdings, then defeat the Palace Marshal at the royal citadel.
